statement: The first line holds n. The next n lines each hold n digits (0 or 1, space-separated): the adjacency matrix of n cities, where 1 means two cities are directly connected; the diagonal is 1. A province is a maximal group of cities reachable from each other. Print the number of provinces. Scan all cities; every time an unvisited one appears, count a new province and let a BFS or DFS swallow its whole group.
constraints: The matrix is symmetric with 1s on the diagonal.

example.why: Cities 0 and 1 connect to each other; city 2 connects only to itself.

hint: The outer loop over all cities is the algorithm; the walk is just the eater.
mistake: Launching one walk from city 0 and reporting what it saw - that counts one province, always.
